decisions.reason: The same-message requirement that high-speed mixing remain smooth rather than overly aggressive is already fully represented in this candidate's existing MODIFY.
The client only identifies bowl-depth adjustment as a conditional splash-mitigation option and does not commit to changing the existing bowl depth or capacity.

The approved 3000 RPM maximum, adjustable range, and intended mixing modes are already fully represented by this candidate's same-message MODIFY; the splash constraint does not further change speed-drive state.
The prohibition on constant maximum-speed operation and the prolonged-use expectation are already represented by this candidate's same-message Event.
The approved motor selection is already represented in the same-message BOM MODIFY, while the possible splash guard and geometry adjustments are conditional and do not necessarily add BOM components.
Accommodation of the approved larger 3000 RPM motors is already represented in the same-message MODIFY, and no specific splash guard, whisk-position, or bowl-depth layout change is mandated.
The source Event concerns splashing during higher-speed mixing, not the separate dispensing flow, valve operation, or post-close dripping behavior.
Controlling splash at higher mixing speeds does not change the existing leak-free plumbing or bowl-bottom seal requirements.
Possible bowl-depth adjustment for splash mitigation does not alter the requirement that bowls be quickly removable and swappable.
The high-speed splash constraint does not modify the existing requirement that seals prevent liquid from entering the base or electronics.
The source decision has no effect on placard text, placement, or customer-facing orientation.
Although higher motor speed could theoretically affect vibration, the source does not change stability behavior or require additional stabilization features.
